title: C#
tagline: From your first line to async, LINQ and beyond.

dreams.title: Sidekick
dreams.pitch: Your own developer assistant: `sk` greets you each morning, keeps your tasks and timers, writes your standup, charts your week and finds anything with a query. Every line of it is code you wrote.
dreams.summary: The sk command line: tasks, timers, standups, weekly charts, search, GitHub import, installed as a .NET tool.
features: `sk`: your banner, a greeting that knows the time and the weekday, your daily goal, what to do next and your streak
`sk add "Fix login" --tag bug --est 45m`, `sk start 1`, `sk stop`, `sk done 1`: tasks and timers that remember
`sk standup`: yesterday / today / blockers, ready to paste into Teams
`sk week`: your week as a bar chart with time per project; `sk timesheet`, `sk invoice`, `sk streak`
`sk find "tag=bug and minutes>30"`: your own query language, compiled to an expression tree
`sk import owner/repo`: open GitHub issues become tasks, page by page; `sk links` fetches page titles in parallel
Installed for real: `dotnet tool install -g` and `sk` works in every terminal

out: |   S I D E K I C K                  v0.1   |
[AL] Good morning, Ada Lovelace. Wednesday 25 November.
- Waiting on API keys from ops

artifact.run: dotnet run -- help   (or any command with --demo); install: dotnet pack, then dotnet tool install -g Sidekick.Dojo --add-source ./nupkg

README.md: # Sidekick
The developer assistant you built yourself, lesson by lesson, in the code-dojo **C#** track.
Every file under `Core/` and most of `Cli/` is your own passing code. Files you have not earned yet are
stubs that say which lesson builds them, so `sk` builds and runs at every stage.
## Run it
```text
dotnet run -- help
dotnet run                          your day: banner, greeting, goal, next tasks, streak
dotnet run -- add "Fix login redirect" --tag bug --est 45m --project web
dotnet run -- start 1               start a timer        dotnet run -- stop
dotnet run -- log 1 09:00-10:30     log time by hand     dotnet run -- done 1
dotnet run -- standup               yesterday / today / blockers, ready to paste in Teams
dotnet run -- week                  your week as a bar chart, time by project
dotnet run -- find "tag=bug and minutes>30"
dotnet run -- standup --demo        any command on sample data, nothing saved
Your data lives in `%USERPROFILE%\.sidekick` (`sidekick.json`, `profile.json`). Set `SIDEKICK_HOME` to use
another folder.
## Install it as a real command
```text
dotnet pack
dotnet tool install -g Sidekick.Dojo --add-source ./nupkg
sk
After a change: `dotnet pack` again, then `dotnet tool update -g Sidekick.Dojo --add-source ./nupkg`.
`sk doctor` checks the tool settings in `sk.csproj`.
## Where each piece comes from
| Folder | What | Built in |
| `Cli/Banner.cs`, `Cli/Tagline.cs` | the banner | First steps |
| `Core/Minutes.cs`, `Core/Duration.cs`, `Core/Slug.cs`, `Core/DayReceipt.cs` | formatting | First steps |
| `Core/Greeting.cs`, `Cli/Commands.cs`, `Cli/Shell.cs`, `Core/Bar.cs`, `Core/Focus.cs` | decisions and loops | Control flow |
| `Core/WeekChart.cs`, `Core/Stats.cs`, `Core/Inbox.cs`, ... | methods and collections | Methods and collections |
| `Core/Model/*`, `Core/Journal.cs`, `Core/Store.cs`, `Core/Assistant.cs` | your task model | Objects and types |
| `Core/Errors.cs`, `Cli/AddArgs.cs`, `Cli/ParseCommand.cs`, `Core/Clock.cs`, `Core/Priority.cs` | robust parsing, dates, priorities | Robust code |
| `Core/Reports/*`, `Core/Filters.cs`, `Core/Recurring.cs` | standup, week, summary | Generics and LINQ |
| `Core/Storage/JsonFileStore.cs`, `Core/Net/*`, `Core/Import/IssuePages.cs` | saving, links, GitHub import | Async and await |
| `Core/Events.cs`, `Cli/Container.cs`, `Cli/CommandAttribute.cs`, `Core/Query/FilterCompiler.cs`, ... | celebrations, DI, help, sk find, sync | Advanced C# |
| `Core/Reports/TopPicks.cs`, `Timesheet.cs`, `Invoice.cs`, `Streak.cs`, `Sessions.cs`, ... | deeper reports | LINQ in depth |
The host (`Program.cs`, `Cli/Host.cs`, `Cli/App.cs`) is the part the dojo gives you: it wires the real clock,
your user folder and `HttpClient` to your pieces.
